Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our end and suggested next steps to keep momentum on the POC: 

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary use case: in-product contextual assistant for customer support (reduce average handle time and automate L2 tasks).
- Decision criteria: latency (<= 300ms for short chats), cost per active session, data residency, and auditability (logs + conversation history).
- Pilot scope: 3 internal teams, ~2000 monthly conversations, 6-week POC.

Stakeholders you mentioned (please confirm / add):
- Economic buyer: Jordan Blake (CTO) — final sign-off on budget
- Technical champion: Claire O'Neil (you) — product/functional owner
- Security & privacy review: Nina Patel (Legal) — DPA / data handling
- Procurement: procurement@acme.com — commercial terms and PO

Legal/contract asks from your side we heard today:
- Acme typically wants an NDA before detailed logs are shared.
- MSA + DPA (data processing addendum) will be reviewed by legal, procurement owns PO.
- Typical routing: NDA -> MSA + DPA -> PO/signature. Turn times can vary.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm stakeholder list and the best contacts for procurement/legal.
2) If you have an NDA draft, send it over and we can circulate our standard NDA. (I've attached our standard NDA for reference.)
3) I'll loop in our SE (Aditya) for a short technical session next week to scope integration points and telemetry requirements.
4) We can prepare a Statement of Work for the 6-week POC once legal routing is clear.

Attachments: Redwood_NDA_template.pdf (attached)

If that all looks right, can we schedule the SE session for Tue or Wed next week?

Thanks —

Marissa / Claire —

Thanks for looping me in. Quick plan from contracts/ops perspective: 

1) NDA review: we can review Acme's NDA and return redlines within 1-2 business days after receipt. If Acme prefers, we can also propose our standard NDA (Redwood_NDA_template.pdf) and push DocuSign; that's often faster when customers don't have heavy bespoke language.

2) MSA + DPA sequencing:
- Best practice: get NDA signed first, then circulate MSA + DPA for legal review.
- If Acme prefers faster parallel review, we can circulate MSA + DPA in parallel with NDA, but we'll ask for a short acknowledgement that NDA comments won't block MSA redlines.

3) Turn times (targeted):
- NDA: 1-2 business days for Redwood to provide comments; once both parties accept, signature in 1 business day via DocuSign.
- MSA: initial redlines from Redwood within 3 business days after we receive the counterparty MSA. Extensive negotiation may take longer depending on customer legal bandwidth.
- DPA: 4-7 business days, can often be completed in parallel to MSA after technical/data requirements are confirmed.

4) Signatory owners: we typically route commercial terms to me / Head of Contracts and VP Legal for signature depending on liability/term thresholds. For smaller POCs, the Head of Sales + Head of Contracts can execute.

DocuSign / HubSpot: I'll upload the NDA/initial SOW to DocuSign and link to the HubSpot deal.

I'll prepare a short email template we can send to Acme legal/procurement with next steps and our DocuSign links. Aditya — please prepare a one-page summary of telemetry/data samples we'll share with legal (no PII) so Nina can confirm the DPA scope.

Ben Carter
